q: I had a panic attack last night because I have to run around with a toddler during the day and I’m running on 4 hours (sometimes less) of sleep and I’m feeling so broken.
cx: Second baby waking every 30 minutes for two months; she also has a toddler to chase all day.

q: she is crying for 2-3 hours straight at times in the middle of the night and if I don’t let her “sleep in” she is hazy red eyes exhausted the next day
cx: Explains why the family sleeps in to 9am: the night holds hours of crying.

q: I’m currently 31 weeks and I can’t sleep due to extreme bodily pain. My legs are aching and sore , my husband rubs them all he can but nothing seems to help.
cx: Second pregnancy; leg and back pain keep her awake; she cannot lift her toddler.

q: I hate feeling so useless. I’ve tried icing the spots, asking for pain killers that are safe, massages, heat, everything I can think of.
cx: Lists everything tried for pregnancy pain that stops her sleeping.

q: I was never a napper as an adult. So sleep when baby sleeps (during the day) was impossible for me. For the first 20 weeks of my baby’s life I probably got 5 hours of sleep max broken up.
cx: First-time mother looking back over the first five months before sleep training.

q: We’re usually in bed 8-9pm and he falls asleep 9:30-10:00. Meanwhile I am staring at the ceiling until midnight or later and I wake up very very often.
cx: Baby now sleeps 7:30-7 after sleep training; she lies awake while her husband sleeps.

q: I don’t know if my body is just primed to waking up hourly because that’s what my baby was doing for 8 weeks during the regression. Is this what insomnia is like?
cx: Her own sleep stays broken after the baby's is fixed.

q: But I’m EXHAUSTED. Somehow I feel more tired than when I was battling bedtime and waking up all night with her.
cx: Weeks after sleep training worked for the baby.

q: I didn’t want to sleep train, but my mental health was deteriorating. Sleep deprivation was causing anxiety, sleep paralysis, auditory hallucinations. It was a scary and sad time for me. I was taking unisom once or twice a week to catch up on sleep.
cx: Why she sleep trained at 20 weeks.

q: When did you start getting restorative sleep again? Any tips to help fall asleep? I EBF my baby so I’m hesitant to take things that might affect my supply or pass to baby. Unisom was a desperate measure.
cx: Asks others when their own sleep came back.

q: I am going to try giving the monitor to my husband to keep on his side and see if that helps.
cx: Her next step for her own sleep after commenters' replies.

q: Yes I’m a super light sleeper now. I used to sleep so deeply my alarm needed to be super loud for me to wake up. Now the slightest noise wakes me up so frustrating.
cx: Agrees with a commenter that motherhood changed how she sleeps.

q: I asked him if he could please take one of the baby’s night feeds tonight, and I would take the other. I specifically chose tonight because he had finished work early and has Sunday off. I rarely ask him for help, and I told him that I’m exhausted and just really needed one feed where I could sleep uninterrupted.
cx: Mother of a toddler and a one-month-old; five weeks without a full night.

q:
He also added that I have help every day from 8–12.  
He also said that the baby “only wakes twice a night.”  
I became really upset because I felt like he was trying to build a case for why I wasn’t actually as exhausted as I said I was.
cx: What her husband told ChatGPT when they asked it to settle the night-feed argument.

q: When I tried explaining why it hurt me, he told me I was “making a mountain out of a molehill.”
cx: Husband's reply when she said his account minimised her exhaustion.

q: When I finally said, “I’m exhausted and I need you to take one feed,” I expected my husband to be in my corner. Instead, I felt like he was explaining to someone else why my exhaustion wasn’t really that significant.
cx: The part of the night-feed fight that hurt most.

q: Yes, the baby only wakes twice. Yes, I have help from 8–12. Yes, I know both of those things are fortunate. I’m still exhausted. I don’t think I need to prove that by explaining that I have my own business or that I struggle to fall back asleep after waking.
cx: Answers commenters who weighed her exhaustion against others' situations.

q: I don’t think exhaustion should have to reach some objective threshold before you’re allowed to ask your partner for help.
cx: Her rule for asking for a night feed.

q: I seem to have a hard time sleeping for longer than about 2 hours if I’m away from my baby. During the first few months postpartum, baby was perfectly fine with Dad, who would take care of him, so technically I could have gotten 3–4 hours of continuous sleep. But I would always wake up after 1-2h at most.
cx: Nine months postpartum; the father covered nights but she still woke.

q: Other times, I would wake up with this sudden feeling that I needed to go check on him, or I would think I heard him crying. Most of the time he actually was crying, but Dad was handling it and would have woken me up if he needed me.
cx: What woke her on the nights her partner had the baby.

q: Sometimes I would wake up scared that the baby was in bed with me under the sheets. I even remember reminding myself out loud before going to sleep that the baby wasn’t in bed with me, so I could relax and sleep.
cx: Early postpartum night waking while the baby was with the father.

q: To be fair, since fully committing to bedsharing, I haven’t really tried sleeping for a long stretch away from him—almost like I haven’t mentally given myself permission to.
cx: Why she still cannot sleep more than two hours apart from the baby.

q: I also used to feel like my body would just wake me up because I needed to feed him, sometimes even with a letdown. I don’t have that strong physical urgency anymore, so I guess my body is still gradually learning to relax and adapt… just very slowly haha.
cx: Her body waking her for feeds, months on.

q: Bedsharing is what currently works best for our family, and for now I’m not looking to sleep train, but I’m definitely open to hearing what has helped other moms with their own sleep!
cx: Pushes back on sleep-training replies; wants help for her own sleep instead.

q: but I’m struggling so much to sleep or rest - my head is constantly thinking about what i am doing right or wrong, i miss my first daughter and our quality time together
cx: Day three after her second birth; parents in town helping.

q: It’s like there are feathers inside just twirling around my legs and feet creating this horrible itchy/tickly/slithery feeling under the skin. I can’t fall asleep or stay asleep. I can’t get comfortable.
cx: Restless legs in pregnancy.

q: Going to ask my doctor about sleep aids at my next visit. Going on a week of only 4 hours of sleep a night and I haven’t been able to nap at all.
cx: A week of restless-leg nights.

q: The thing is when my husband brought our toddler over to his dad’s for a sleepover I woke up feeling great. I didn’t want to disrupt my sleep schedule so I slept the same amount I always do 10:30-7. […] The second she gets back, boom exhausted again. What does this mean?
cx: Always tired whatever the hours; one night with the toddler away changed it.

q: He will not sleep in his cot from 3-4am (its been this way since about 6 weeks) so he sleeps on me in the recliner chair and I just sit there whilst he sleeps.
cx: Almost six months; studio flat, cot beside her, breastfeeding.
r: safe sleep (baby sleeping on her in a recliner)

q: I'm sorry this is so all over the place but I've barely slept in 3 weeks and crying on and off.
cx: End of a post that opens by naming postpartum depression.
